rejected.title: Texts represent values
card: Values are what a person or group believes is right, fair or important. Examples include honesty, loyalty, fairness and care for others.
A literary text can show values through what characters do and say, and through what the story rewards or punishes.
The ideas and points of view in a text can also show the values of a character, a group or the author. These may differ from each other.
To find a value, ask what the text treats as good or bad, and what evidence in the text supports your reading.
rejected.remember: Look at what a text rewards, punishes and treats as important to find its values.

a.q: In a story, Priya returns a lost wallet and is thanked by the whole town. Which value does the story show as important?
opts: Honesty
Wealth
Popularity
Luck
a.why: Priya is rewarded for doing the right thing with something that is not hers, which shows the story treats honesty as important. Popularity is tempting because the town thanks her, but that is the result of her act, not the value being shown.
a.clue: What does Priya do with the wallet, and how does the story treat it?

b.q: In a short story, Leo hides a mistake his teammates made, to protect them. When the truth comes out, the whole team stops trusting him. What value does the story most likely suggest?
opts: Honesty matters more than covering for friends
Covering for friends matters more than honesty
Protecting the team matters more than the truth
Hiding mistakes is the best way to keep trust
b.why: The story punishes Leo's choice to hide the mistake: he loses the team's trust. That suggests the story treats honesty as more important. Putting loyalty first is tempting because Leo acts to protect his friends, but the ending shows the story does not reward that choice.
b.clue: Look at what happens to Leo at the end, not just what he does.
